title: Every machine's unchanged manifest and media tree are deleted and rewritten in full every 10 minutes
what: The companion force-resends local_manifest and media_tree every 600 s even when unchanged, and the dashboard answers each resend with DELETE + re-INSERT of up to 4,000 editor_media and 4,000 media_tree_clips rows per ticked project. The rewrite also bumps editor_media_project.reported_at, which invalidates the owed-files cache fingerprint.
cost: Measured per ticked project, unchanged: 27.5 ms + 0.84 MB WAL (manifest) and 30.6 ms + 0.80 MB WAL (media tree). Today ~40 project-ticks: ~9.5 GB/day written for no change. At 20 machines x 10 ticks: 0.55 MB/s, ~47 GB/day, ~11.6 s write-lock time per 10 min; both tables (156 + 147 MB) rewritten several times an hour, pinned by hourly snapshots (estimated).
evidence: Probe on a 20-machine fill of the real schema (populate.py / probe.py in the scratch folder); the report handler has no digest or compare before calling replace.
fix: Store a per-project digest on editor_media_project (and for the media tree); skip the replace when unchanged and touch only the small row; prune big-table rows via the small row by PK prefix; fingerprint the owed cache on the digest. Keep the 600 s resend.

title: Overlapping long backlog reads can starve WAL checkpoints, and the WAL file never shrinks
where: dashboard/src/ccsync_dashboard/db.py:710-728 (connect: no journal_size_limit or checkpoint policy); readers db.py:11845 via ui_home.py:423 and ui.py:1870
what: The WAL restarts only when no reader holds a snapshot using it. The admin backlog read takes ~0.9 s at 20 machines here (6 s at 50 editors per PL-RES-74) and is polled every 2 s per tab; continuous overlap makes every commit append. No journal_size_limit, so the -wal file keeps its high-water size.
cost: Probe: one replace every 50 ms with 2 overlapping readers grew the WAL to 549 MB in 45 s (0 readers: 5 MB). At today's cadence and query speed it stayed 6-8 MB, so it needs 20+ machines on NAS CPU or 3+ admin tabs; then ~2 GB/hour of /data at the dash-db-1 write rate, never returned.
evidence: walstarve.py and walstarve_real.py in the scratch folder.
fix: PRAGMA journal_size_limit (e.g. 64 MB) in connect; collector runs wal_checkpoint(RESTART) with a bounded wait each prune cycle and logs an oversized WAL. Shortening the reads (PL-RES-74) removes the overlap.

title: editor_media and media_tree_clips store a long TEXT composite key twice (rowid table + autoindex)
what: Rowid tables with a composite TEXT PRIMARY KEY keep the row and a full copy of the key in sqlite_autoindex; every lookup and replace touches both b-trees.
cost: At 20 machines x 10 ticks: editor_media 156.2 -> 100.8 MB WITHOUT ROWID (-35%), one project replace 15.7 -> 12.6 ms (-20%); media_tree_clips 146.6 -> 120.7 MB (-18%), 19.8 -> 17.3 ms. nas_media is not a candidate (178 -> 217 MB).
fix: One migration step rebuilding both tables WITHOUT ROWID; since both are full-replace caches repopulated within 10 minutes, the step can recreate them empty, keeping boot cost near zero.

title: The hourly prune full-scans the largest tables while holding the write lock
what: EXPLAIN shows SCAN for editor_media/media_tree_clips/missing_files/editor_media_project by refreshed_at, lane_report_history (no index), transfer_history by received_at (indexed on completed_at), completion_history twice with a temp b-tree, and nas_media NOT IN (800k rows), all in one transaction committed afterwards.
cost: Hourly; 352 ms steady state at the 20-machine fill on NVMe (1-2 s on NAS estimated), blocking every writer meanwhile; linear in machines x ticks.
evidence: Query plans and timing from probe.py.
fix: Delete media rows by PK prefix for stale editor_media_project pairs; purge nas_media only for inactive project ids; prune transfer_history on an indexed column; commit between groups. Do not index editor_media.refreshed_at.

title: lane_report_history and completion_history are written and pruned but nothing displays them
what: No route, template or alert reads either table; the only readers are the person-data export/purge, the machine rename and upsert_completion reading its own last row.
cost: ~200 extra SELECTs/min at 20 machines x 10 ticks in the collector, the hourly thinning GROUP BY over ~170k rows, ~72k lane rows/month, plus schema/export/prune surface.
evidence: grep of both table names across dashboard/src.
fix: Give them a reader (per-lane state timeline) or stop writing and drop them in a migration, updating the export table list.

title: The home page computes the fleet backlog three times per render, and each pair's download diff twice
what: One admin GET / runs fetch_sync_backlog three times (600 originals queries for 200 pairs, 9 connections, 2,793 statements); within it the proxy NOT EXISTS anti-join runs once for totals and again for the 50 names.
cost: 20-machine fill on this desktop: GET / 2.8 s; /partials/home-transfers 0.91 s and /partials/transfers 1.0 s, each polled every 2 s; 99% of fetch_sync_backlog time is SQL. Today ~170 ms per call.
evidence: trace_pages.py and profile_backlog.py in the scratch folder.
fix: As part of PL-RES-74: compute once per request and pass it down; fetch totals and first 50 names in one pass with window aggregates.
